newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS -Moody's boosts the Philippines.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS -Moody's boosts the Philippines.

text.p: Sovereign bonds of the Philippines tightened a few basis points on news that Moody's Investors Service had raised the country's foreign currency debt ratings, traders said on Monday.
Asian debt markets also offered a few new issues, with Guangdong Development Bank launching a US$50 million FRCD and Malaysian Airlines bringing a 10 billion yen FRN.
The bond issue for the Republic of the Philippines due in 2016 tightened three to four basis points to trade at 174 to 176 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries, traders said.
"The bulk of the trade was done at 176 and 175, but we did do a trade at the tighter end of the range," said one trader.
Moody's raised the Philippines' foreign currency bond rating to Ba1 from Ba2 and its foreign currency deposit rating to Ba2 from Ba3.
The Philippines sovereign bond issue, which was sold in exchange for Philippine Brady bonds in September 1996, was priced to yield 225 basis points over the benchmark.
Since then, its spread has tightened considerably amid growing optimism over the Philippines' economic outlook.
For example, bond spreads tightened in February when Standard and Poor's Corp raised the Philippines' sovereign rating to BB-plus from BB.

Philippine bond spreads widened, however, along with other high-yielding paper in March amid expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve would tighten monetary policy. That expectation was borne out when the Fed raised the key federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 percent on March 25.
The Philippines sovereign bond was trading at around 190 basis points in March, traders said.
Traders said some other Philippine bonds traded in the secondary market were mostly steady after today's ratings news.
Andrew Alcid, head of capital markets at Citibank in Manila, said the Moody's upgrade came at a good time for the country.
"There has been a lot of comparison with Thailand and there was a lot of speculation about what's going to happen with the (Philippine) economy," said Alcid.
"Moody's just confirmed that the fundamentals in the Philippines are pretty sound and that people should not be too overly concerned about what is going on here," he said.
Bankers said the rating upgrade is good news for the Philippines central bank, which still plans to launch a bond into the U.S. market.

The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas planned to launch a long-dated Yankee issue in mid-April but decided after consultations with the issue's management group to postpone the deal because of poor market conditions.

"The upgrade will certainly help the issue," said a banker in Hong Kong. But he said the Philippines, like other prospective bond issuers, will be waiting to see what happens at this week's meeting of the Fed's policymaking committee.
The Federal Open Market Committee meets on May 20.
In other news, Pakistan is expected to launch its three-year floating rate note issue on Tuesday.
And Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand has mandated BA Asia and Nomura International (Hong Kong) Ltd to arrange a US$150 million floating rate note issue.
